h: Company facts
t: # Ezydrag > Ezydrag is an AI agent studio in India. We design, build and run AI agents for revenue teams (sales, marketing and RevOps), inside the tools they already use: CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot, Attio), marketing automation (Marketo, HubSpot), data (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks), workflows (n8n, MCP servers, APIs) and Slack, Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace. A person on the client's team approves every important step. Key facts: Model: a service, not software. We build, run and improve the agents. Flagship: Sales Nurture Agent (capture, enrich, score, nurture, meeting, won). Portfolio: Email Creation Agent, Email QA Agent, QBR Generator, AI PTA, Voice Agent (with Nutaan AI), Ask Ezydrag, Prospecting Agent, Governance Agent. Built to order: Speed-to-Lead, Churn and Upsell, Deal Follow-up, CRM Cleanup, Forecasting, Deal Desk, Attribution agents. Agents never negotiate prices and never send important messages without approval. Legal name: Ezydrag Private Limited. Offices: Kolkata, Bangalore, Durgapur. Contact: hello@ezydrag.in

h: Ezydrag / Why watching an AI work makes you trust it more (yes, it's psychology)…
t: People trust what they can see being done. It's called the labor illusion. Agents take minutes, not milliseconds, so show the real work, step by step. Never fake it. Santanu Mondal Director of Design · 9 Nov 2026 · 2 min read #sales #salesforce #agents

h: Ezydrag / Every CRM now ships an SDR agent. So… what's your edge?
t: Salesforce made a lead-nurture agent a standard feature. When everyone has the same agent, the edge is your rules, your content, your approvals and who runs it. Shuvam Santra & Anirban Dasgupta Chief Technology Officer · Chief Operating Officer · 9 Nov 2026 · 2 min read #n8n #agents #workflows

h: Ezydrag / Workflow or agent? Stop overthinking it. Take the 2-minute test…
t: If you can list the steps, it's a workflow. If each step depends on the last answer, it's an agent. Most real jobs are both. Take the quiz below. Shuvam Santra & Anirban Dasgupta Chief Technology Officer · Chief Operating Officer · 9 Nov 2026 · 2 min read

h: The Ezydrag Report 2026
t: Home The 2026 Report Following up with AI: field notes. What we learned running AI agents on real leads in Marketo and Salesforce. Free to read. No form. 6 chapters 6 Nov 2026 ~9 min read 1 · The busywork tax 2 · Context beats prompts 3 · Approval is a feature 4 · Tokens are the new cloud bill 5 · Privacy deadlines are product deadlines 6 · What we're building next How we wrote this This isn't a survey. It's what a small team noticed while building and running agents for real sales and marketing teams, written down so you can skip a few of our mistakes. CHAPTER 1

h: The Ezydrag Report 2026 / The busywork tax
t: Ask a marketing ops lead what fills their week and you rarely hear "strategy." You hear lists that arrive in five formats, emails stitched together block by block, last-minute QA, and a quarterly deck rebuilt from spreadsheets. None of it is hard. All of it is careful, repetitive and easy to get slightly wrong. That combination is exactly where agents help, and exactly where a careless agent hurts. CHAPTER 2

h: The Ezydrag Report 2026 / Context beats prompts
t: Our early agents had clever prompts and poor results. The model wasn't the problem. The agent simply couldn't see that the contact in Marketo was the same person with an open deal in Salesforce, or that someone promised her pricing in Tuesday's meeting. An agent is only as good as what it can see. So we stopped tuning prompts and started connecting things. Accounts, contacts, campaigns, deals, meeting notes and policies now live in one context graph. Agents ask the graph, get a small set of connected facts, and cite where each fact came from. CHAPTER 3

h: The Ezydrag Report 2026 / Approval is a feature, not friction
t: Fully autonomous agents make good demos and nervous customers. In practice, the teams we work with want the agent to do the work and a person to make the call. So every send and every sync waits for a named person. That one click turned out to matter more than any model upgrade: it is why teams let agents near real customers at all. Each approval is logged, so "who sent this?" always has an answer. CHAPTER 4

h: The Ezydrag Report 2026 / Tokens are the new cloud bill
t: Agents that paste whole exports into a prompt are slow and expensive, and the useful signal gets buried. Costs creep up quietly, one agent at a time. Three habits keep the bill flat: send connected facts instead of exports, answer known questions from approved Q&A with no model call at all, and let an optimization agent watch the others and suggest cuts. You can try the calculator with your own numbers. CHAPTER 5

h: The Ezydrag Report 2026 / Privacy deadlines are product deadlines
t: India's DPDP Rules were notified on 13 November 2025, with full compliance due by 13 May 2027. Many of our clients also serve EU users under GDPR. The hard part isn't the law. It's knowing where personal data lives. The same graph that helps agents also answers that question, which is why we treat compliance as part of the product rather than a separate audit. More in our compliance guide . CHAPTER 6

h: The Ezydrag Report 2026 / What we're building next
t: Lead routing and scoring, weekly campaign insights that feed the QBR, inbound inquiry replies, and ongoing data hygiene. Each one starts the same way: one workflow, one owner, one clear measure of done. If you're running RevOps on Marketo and Salesforce and any of this sounds familiar, we'd like to hear what your week looks like.

h: The Ezydrag Report 2026 / How we wrote this
t: Edition 01 is written from our own delivery work, including the agents we run with RightWave. It contains no survey data and no third-party statistics. Where we cite a date or a rule, it's a public one. Future editions will add measured results once our clients approve publishing them. Field Notes

h: FAQ: What does Ezydrag do?
t: What does Ezydrag do? We're an AI agent studio. We design, build and run AI agents for revenue teams, inside the tools they already use. A person on your team approves every important step.

h: FAQ: Which agents have you built?
t: Which agents have you built? The Sales Nurture Agent (our flagship), Email Creation, Email QA, QBR Generator, AI PTA, a Voice Agent built with Nutaan AI, a Prospecting Agent, a Governance Agent that logs and approves what the others do, and Ask Ezydrag, which you're talking to now.

h: FAQ: Can you build a custom agent?
t: Can you build a custom agent? Yes. Tell us the task your team repeats. We'll tell you honestly whether an agent should do it, then build, test and run it with you.

h: FAQ: Is Ezydrag software we have to learn?
t: Is Ezydrag software we have to learn? No. We're a service. Our team builds and runs the agents inside your existing tools, so there's no new platform to learn.

h: FAQ: Which tools do your agents work with?
t: Which tools do your agents work with? Whatever your team already runs: CRMs like Salesforce, HubSpot and Attio; Marketo and HubSpot for marketing; Clay and Apollo for data; n8n for workflows; Slack, Google Workspace and Microsoft 365; and warehouses like Snowflake, BigQuery and Databricks. If a tool has an API or an MCP server, we can usually connect it. We confirm the exact list during scoping.

h: FAQ: What tools are GTM teams actually using in 2026?
t: What tools are GTM teams actually using in 2026? In a July 2026 survey of 62 GTM leaders, the most common tools were Clay (71%), n8n (48%), HubSpot (39%), Apollo (35%) and Attio (32%). Small sample, but a useful signal: data enrichment and workflow automation now sit at the centre of the stack.

h: FAQ: Is our data ready for AI agents?
t: Is our data ready for AI agents? Most companies aren't sure, and it matters. Gartner predicts that through 2026, organisations will abandon 60% of AI projects unsupported by AI-ready data. In a Gartner survey, 63% of organisations said they don't have, or aren't sure they have, the right data management practices for AI. That's why every Ezydrag project starts with a data check.

h: FAQ: Why does metadata matter for AI agents?
t: Why does metadata matter for AI agents? Because an agent needs to know what a field means, where it came from and who's allowed to see it. Gartner's 2025 Magic Quadrant for Metadata Management calls metadata "the indispensable foundation for modern and agentic AI systems". Without it, agents guess. With it, they can show their reasons.

h: FAQ: Where is the data stack heading?
t: Where is the data stack heading? Toward open formats that many tools can share. In a January 2026 survey of 252 senior data leaders (commissioned by Ryft, a vendor), 58% used Apache Iceberg for business-critical analytics, 95% used or planned to use it for AI and ML, and 79% planned to move their remaining data to it within 12 months. For agents, open formats mean less copying and one source of truth.

h: FAQ: How do agents connect to our systems safely?
t: How do agents connect to our systems safely? Through narrow tools with narrow access. Many tools now use the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Its 28 July 2026 spec made it stateless, so any request can reach any server, and it hardened authorisation. We start read-only and the agent never holds your keys.

h: FAQ: Do you work with Snowflake, BigQuery or Databricks?
t: Do you work with Snowflake, BigQuery or Databricks? Usually, yes. We read from your warehouse with the access you grant, and we prefer using your existing definitions and metadata over copying data into new places. We confirm the details during scoping.

h: FAQ: How do you test agents before they go live?
t: How do you test agents before they go live? We break them on purpose. Research published in August 2026 (AgentChaos) injected faults like timeouts and wrong values into agent systems: every system got worse, with success dropping by up to 50 points. Robustness depended more on how the system was built than on the model. So we run every agent through a failure list, and a pass means it stopped and told a person.

h: FAQ: What is an agent harness?
t: What is an agent harness? Everything around the model: context, tools, memory, checks and logs. Addy Osmani put it simply: "A decent model with a great harness beats a great model with a bad harness." Most of our build time goes into the harness.

h: FAQ: Why do so many agentic AI projects fail?
t: Why do so many agentic AI projects fail? Gartner predicts more than 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by the end of 2027, citing rising costs, unclear business value and weak risk controls. Our answer: one task, one measurable goal, a person on every key step, and a team that stays to run it.

h: FAQ: How do you monitor agents in production?
t: How do you monitor agents in production? We log every step, tool call and approval, then review the runs. Researchers call this the agent's trajectory and argue it's the right basis for testing and debugging agents in production.

h: FAQ: Which RevOps agents have the clearest ROI?
t: Which RevOps agents have the clearest ROI? The ones tied to a number you can check: speed-to-lead (response time), prospecting (meetings booked) and churn-and-upsell (revenue saved). It matters because proof is rare: Default's H1 2026 research found fewer than 10% of RevOps leaders had seen AI contribute directly to pipeline.

h: FAQ: Will AI agents negotiate with our customers?
t: Will AI agents negotiate with our customers? Not ours. And the market agrees: in a Q4 2026 benchmark of 102 RevOps practitioners, only 6% will let AI agents negotiate with customers in the next 12 months, and 75% said no. Pricing and negotiation stay with a person.

h: FAQ: How should we budget for AI agent running costs?
t: How should we budget for AI agent running costs? Per outcome, not per token. Vendors are adding meters: Atlassian will charge for excess Rovo credits ($0.01 each) and automation steps from 3 December 2026, with overage on by default. We estimate costs before a pilot and report them per lead, email or report after.

h: FAQ: Will AI agents replace our SDR team?
t: Will AI agents replace our SDR team? No. They take the follow-up work so reps can sell. Salesforce's February 2026 survey found 55% of sales professionals already use AI for prospecting. The edge now is your rules, your content and who runs the agent.

h: FAQ: Which agents are companies building next?
t: Which agents are companies building next? Research and reporting agents top the list: 56% of organisations plan to build them in the next 12 months, according to Anthropic's 2026 State of AI Agents survey of 500+ technical leaders. Our QBR Generator does exactly that job.

h: FAQ: What's a good first agent for a portfolio company?
t: What's a good first agent for a portfolio company? Pick one job with a clear number: CRM cleanup (duplicates and missing fields fixed) or speed-to-lead (response time). Both are quick to measure and make every later agent better.

h: FAQ: Do we approve what the agents do?
t: Do we approve what the agents do? Yes. Important actions, like sending an email or changing a record, wait for a named person on your team. Every approval is logged.

h: FAQ: What happens when an agent is unsure?
t: What happens when an agent is unsure? It stops and asks a person. Unclear cases go to a review list, not out the door.

h: FAQ: How do you protect our data?
t: How do you protect our data? Limited, read-only access to start, encryption on every connection, a written data agreement and deletion whenever you ask.

h: FAQ: Do your agents respect consent?
t: Do your agents respect consent? Yes. Agents only contact people who have given consent, and we check your setup against GDPR, India's DPDP Act and HIPAA where they apply.

h: FAQ: How do we start?
t: How do we start? Book a 30-minute call. We pick one task and one measure with you, then run a pilot with your approvals in place.

h: FAQ: Do you train our team?
t: Do you train our team? Yes. A short handover, plus hands-on lessons in Ezydrag Academy (in beta).

h: FAQ: How much does it cost?
t: How much does it cost? Every engagement is scoped and priced up front, in writing. Most teams start with a pilot of one agent on one task.

h: FAQ: How do you measure success?
t: How do you measure success? With a number you can check yourself: lead response time, meetings booked, forecast accuracy, churn saved or discount leakage. We agree one before we start.

h: FAQ: Who is Ezydrag?
t: Who is Ezydrag? A small AI agent studio in India. We build and run AI agents for revenue teams, and we stay to keep improving them.

h: FAQ: Where are you based?
t: Where are you based? Kolkata, Bangalore and Durgapur. Our clients are in India, the US, the UK and the EU.

h: FAQ: How do you keep up with AI agent trends?
t: How do you keep up with AI agent trends? We read the published research and listen to the teams we work with. Our Field Notes blog shares what we are seeing, always with sources, and the agents teams ask for most are on our Agents page.
